messages.author: 42e5316f884713d9
messages.subject: Where/how to report package issues?
parts:
Hi, i found a difference in behavior for the downloader package

The following works in GNU R
library(downloader)
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/genomicsclass/dagdata/master/inst/extdata/femaleControlsPopulation.csv"
filename <- basename(url)
download(url, destfile=filename)

But in Renjin Studio (and in the scriptengine) it gives the following error:
Renjin 0.9.2716
Copyright (C) 2018 The R Foundation for Statistical Computing
Copyright (C) 2018 BeDataDriven

library(downloader)
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/genomicsclass/dagdata/master/inst/extdata/femaleControlsPopulation.csv"
filename <- basename(url)
download(url, destfile=filename)
Error: missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

What would be the best procedure to report this? Should i open an issue at https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/issues or somewhere else?

would it help if hamcrest tests accompany the diff?

if so, should those tests be submitted as pull requests somewhere (I did not find a "natural" place for this in the renjin repo, although test-packages seems to be a reasonable place)?

Best regards,
Per

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Where/how to report package issues?
parts:
Hi Per,

In general, the difference in behavior won't lie with a package itself, but rather some part of Renjin itself (base, stats, graphics, etc). 

I dug into the example above and found that the download() function calls if(capabilities("libcurl")) which fails indirectly because we hadn't added the "libcurl" capability to Renjin yet. Because the result is a zero-length vector, the if statement evaluation fails.

The most helpful would be to post this kind of bug and test case to the Renjin project, though I understand that it's not always easy to identify the root cause of a problem affecting a package.

The next best thing is to open a place holder bug mentioning the package, and we'll rename the issue once the root cause is identified. But it may take longer to fix in this case.

Best,
Alex
